title: AI PANORAMA weekly price and specification snapshot
description: The shape of one dated snapshot file in pipeline/snapshots/openrouter/. Required by bible/part-02.md section 2.8, which fixes the shape, and owned by bible/part-09.md section 9.4, which explains why the archive exists at all: release dates are public history, but what a model cost on a particular past Tuesday is recorded nowhere retrievable, so we quietly save the Tuesdays. These files are the frozen evidence and are never edited or deleted; the Neo4j copy is a convenience rebuilt from them. A companion example lives next to this file as price-snapshot.example.json.

schema_version.description: Bumped only when the shape changes. Old files keep their old number and are never rewritten to match (bible LAW 12).

snapshot_date.description: The day this picture of the market was taken, in the machine's local calendar day. Also the file's own name.

taken_at_utc.description: The exact moment of the fetch, in UTC. Two clocks are kept deliberately (bible/part-02.md): the day it belongs to, and the instant it happened.

source_api.description: The precise address the numbers came from, so any claim built on them can be traced to its source (bible LAW 7).

license_of_data.description: Under what terms these numbers were obtained. Recorded on every row too, because the archive is published later as a public dataset (bible/part-09.md 9.4.3).

row_count.description: How many rows the file holds. Stated separately so that a truncated file is obvious rather than silent.

rows.description: One row per model per provider. A model missing from a later file is not deleted from earlier ones: disappearance is itself history.

row.title: One model's price and specification on one day
row.description: MISSING DATA IS MISSING, NEVER ZERO. Every price and specification field is nullable on purpose: a null means nobody published the number, while a zero means genuinely free. Confusing the two would turn an honest gap into a false claim, which bible/part-02.md 2.8 forbids in as many words.

provider.description: Who was selling it. Part of the row's identity, because the same model costs different amounts at different sellers.

model.description: The entity id this row PROPOSES for the model. It is a proposal, not a fact: bible/part-02.md 2.4 forbids silently creating entities, because near-duplicate entities are the disease that killed other knowledge bases. It becomes real only when Nir approves it.

model_is_proposed_entity.description: True while the entity above is still waiting for Nir's approval.

openrouter_model_id.description: The seller's own permanent identifier. Together with provider and snapshot_date this is the row's unique key, enforced by the database.

canonical_slug.description: The seller's dated internal name for this exact variant, useful for spotting a silent model swap.

display_name.description: The human-readable name as published by the seller.

developer_hint.description: Who appears to have made it, as a HINT only. Never treated as a verified fact about the world.

usd_per_m_input.description: Dollars per million tokens read in. Null means not published; 0 means genuinely free.

usd_per_m_output.description: Dollars per million tokens written out.

context_tokens.description: How much the model can hold in mind at once.

throughput_tps_median.description: Tokens per second, median. Left null unless the project measured it ITSELF through its own real usage; a seller's own speed claim is not evidence.

latency_s_p50.description: Seconds to first answer, median, measured the same honest way as throughput above.

modality.description: What goes in and what comes out, for example text->text.

supported_parameters.description: Kept in the file as evidence but deliberately NOT copied into the database, because it is a long list nothing queries. The file is the truth; the database holds what gets asked.

openrouter_created_unix.description: When the seller first listed it, as they report it.
